### CVE-2017-2608
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2018-05-15 | Updated: 2024-08-05 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-502 CWE-502
- CVSS 3.0 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Jenkins before versions 2.44, 2.32.2 is vulnerable to a remote code execution vulnerability involving the deserialization of various types in javax.imageio in XStream-based APIs (SECURITY-383).

- [UNKNOWN] / jenkins: affected jenkins 2.44; affected jenkins 2.32.2

### CVE-2017-1000353
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2018-01-29 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2025-10-02, ransomware=Unknown — Jenkins Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 41965: CloudBees Jenkins 2.32.1 - Java Deserialization (dos/java, 2017-05-05, verified=0)

Jenkins versions 2.56 and earlier as well as 2.46.1 LTS and earlier are vulnerable to an unauthenticated remote code execution. An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability allowed attackers to transfer a serialized Java `SignedObject` object to the Jenkins CLI, that would be deserialized using a new `ObjectInputStream`, bypassing the existing blacklist-based protection mechanism. We're fixing this issue by adding `SignedObject` to the blacklist. We're also backporting the new HTTP CLI protocol from Jenkins 2.54 to LTS 2.46.2, and deprecating the remoting-based (i.e. Java serialization) CLI protocol, disabling it by default.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a
